§6BTX§f

§aBenzene, Toluene, Xylene - the aromatic feedstock that gates hard plastic and fullerene!§f

BTX is a flammable, combustible, viscous, polluting liquid at §e3.15 MTU§f and §e7.87 MHE§f per bucket. It is produced by fractionating §bReformate§f or §bDesulfurized Naphtha§f in the §bFractioning Tower§f.

§6Production§f:
§b•§f §e100mB§f Reformate → §e60mB§f BTX + §e40mB§f Aromatic Hydrocarbons.
§b•§f §e100mB§f Desulfurized Naphtha → §e60mB§f BTX + §e40mB§f High-Octane Diesel.

§6Uses§f:
§b•§f Hard Plastic (Chemical Plant): §e500mB§f BTX + §e500mB§f Phosgene → §e1×§f Hard Plastic Bar.
§b•§f Crystalline Fullerite (Ore Acidizer): §e1,000mB§f BTX + §e4×§f Fullerene.
§b•§f Cracking Tower: §e100mB§f → §e80mB§f Aromatic Hydrocarbons + §e20mB§f Petroleum Gas.

§ePS:§f BTX is the primary gate to §bHard Plastic§f, which enables the §bCatalytic Converter§f, which in turn enables the §bCatalytic Reformer§f and §bHydrotreater§f. Keep a steady BTX supply by dedicating a Fractioning Tower to Reformate processing!
